basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 8.' and it opens 'Vers. 8. Deficiens mortuus est. Beatus Hieronymus dicit hoc male additum scriptorum'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 8. Deficiens mortuus est. Beatus Hieronymus dicit hoc male additum scriptorum vitio. Neque enim defectus vel imminutio justo viro convenit, cum potius augeri et multiplicari debeat Psalmista dicente: Justus ut cedrus Libani multiplicabitur (Psal. XCI, | 13). Plenus dierum. Plenitudo in ortu, actu et obitu sanctorum solet inveniri. Et ideo recte Abraham plenus dierum mortuus fuisse legitur, consummatus et perfectus erat omnibus virtutibus. Econtra in reprobis omnia quadam imperfectione notantur. Unde et psalmus: Viri sanguinum et dolosi non dimidiabunt dies suos (Psal. LIV, 24).-- Congregatus est ad populum suum, id est ad multitudinem praecedentium patrum.
